ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: International Companies Act 1988 (as amended) and the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007 (as amended); beneficial ownership disclosure is governed by the International Companies (Beneficial Ownership) Regulations issued under the ICA, together with the Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) Directions and FATF-aligned Samoa AML/CFT National Action Plan.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all proposed shareholders, directors, officers, UBOs, and authorized signatories against the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, US Department of Commerce Entity List, UK HMT Sanctions List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and Samoa's domestic FIU watchlist and sanctions designations. A commercially available PEP solution must be used to identify politically exposed persons, their family members and close associates. Any PEP, sanction, or adverse media hit requires enhanced due diligence (EDD), additional source-of-wealth and source-of-funds evidence, and escalation to the Registered Agent's MLRO/Compliance Officer. Screening is performed at client onboarding, during periodic EDD reviews, and on a continuous sanctions-change basis.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) Companies Registry Name Reservation e-Service (exclusive filing via SIFA-licensed Registered Agents)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Official registry languages are English and Samoan. An International Company name must be in the Roman alphabet; if the name is proposed in a non-Latin script, a Latin-script transliteration and an English/Samoan translation must be provided and certified by a qualified translator. The legal name must end with a prescribed suffix, such as 'International', 'Limited', 'Ltd', 'Corporation', 'Inc.', or equivalent, consistent with section 21 of the International Companies Act 1988.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Red Cross / Red Crescent / Rotary / Lions (protected marks)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Name reservations are granted for 30 calendar days and may be extended once for an additional 30 days upon payment of the applicable SIFA fee, provided no conflicting name has been registered. In the event of a name rejection, the applicant, through the licensed Registered Agent, must file a written appeal with the Registrar of International Companies within 14 days of receipt of the rejection notice; the appeal must include the original reservation reference, proposed corrected name, evidence of consent from any relevant minister (if a sensitive token is involved), and confirmation of non-conflict with the register. The Registrar must determine the appeal within 21 days. A further rejection may be challenged by way of an application for judicial review before the Supreme Court of Samoa under the Judicature Act. Name clearance and any appeal must be concluded before incorporation; if rejected after reservation, a fresh application with the revised name is required.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A registered office in Samoa at the address of a licensed Registered Agent is statutorily required for each International Company. The agent may operate a 'virtual office' service whereby no staff are dedicated to the client's physical operations; this is fully permissible for a non-resident ISIC 4659 wholesaler that conducts sales, servicing and administration outside Samoa. All regulatory notices and service of process are handled by the agent. The company must, however, maintain board minutes and resolutions outside Samoa and refrain from exercising management control in Samoa, otherwise SIFA may treat it as a resident tax-exempt company with additional substance obligations.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (<5% per annum) for a non-resident International Company with no local physical business activity. The risk escalates to approximately 20% if the company triggers AML/CFT red flags (PEP connection, sanctions screening hit, high-risk geographic exposure, unusual transaction volumes), or if SIFA/FIU receives a mutual legal assistance or tax exchange request. SIFA's inspection practice is primarily desk-based; unannounced physical inspections are targeted only to companies with credible substance or suspicious activity indicators.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1987 (as consolidated), ss. 5-7 (Incorporation), s. 56 (Registered Office), ss. 75-76 (Directors and Officers).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), Apia, Samoa.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Memorandum and Articles of Association accompanied by the prescribed Application for Incorporation of an International Company.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is prescribed; the company may issue one or more shares with or without par value. No escrow account or capital deposit is required for incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT: (1) the Memorandum and Articles of Association as submitted be and are hereby adopted; (2) the subscriber shall accept the allotment of one ordinary share of US$1.00, issued at par to the founding shareholder; (3) the registered office of the Company be established at the office of the registered agent in Apia, Samoa, and the registered agent be appointed; (4) the initial directors be appointed to hold office pursuant to the Articles; (5) the directors elect a Chairperson, a Secretary and a Treasurer; (6) such officers are authorized to open bank accounts, execute account opening documentation, file all statutory returns, and take all necessary actions to commence business; and (7) any two directors may sign cheques and contracts on behalf of the Company.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) via licensed international company registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit two proposed company names in order of preference to the Registrar of International Companies through a licensed SIFA agent. The agent verifies that the name is not identical or misleadingly similar to an existing registered company and that it does not contain restricted words such as 'Bank', 'Trust' or 'Insurance' unless a special license is held. Upon approval, the name reservation is noted for a period of 30 days.
required_dossiers: Identity and due-diligence documents of the proposed shareholder and directors
Certified copy of passport of each proposed beneficial owner
Bank and professional references (where requested by the agent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for similarity or restricted terms, the agent resubmits an alternative name within 24 hours; if the objection is based on insufficient due-diligence documents, supplemental KYC information is filed with SIFA for redetermination.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and execution of constitutive documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered agent and notary public (or subscribing director as permitted under the International Companies Act)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The registered agent prepares the Memorandum and Articles of Association conforming to the International Companies Act 1987, including object clauses permitting the wholesale remarketing of secondhand construction excavators and related heavy machinery. The founding shareholder executes the Memorandum before a witness; the registered agent countersigns. A notarized certificate of good standing of the corporate shareholder (if any) and declarations of solvency are attached.
required_dossiers: Executed Memorandum and Articles of Association
Certificate of incorporation and good standing of corporate shareholder (if any)
Power of attorney appointing the registered agent
Declaration of non-resident status and intended tax exemption
Consent of the proposed directors to act
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar requires amendments to the objects or share provisions, counsel files a revised draft via the agent; if execution defects are identified, the document is re-executed and re-notarized at no additional regulatory cost.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of application and payment of statutory fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), Registrar of International Companies
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The registered agent files the Application for Incorporation electronically through the SIFA portal, attaching the executed Memorandum and Articles, the registered office confirmation, and the consent of the registered agent. The USD 100 incorporation fee is paid via wire transfer or debit from the agent's SIFA trust account. The Registrar issues a certificate of incorporation within the SLA, assigning a unique IC registration number.
required_dossiers: Application for Incorporation of an International Company (Form 1)
Consent of registered agent and registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried due to incomplete supporting documents, the agent files the missing KYC or consent items within 5 business days; if the Registrar issues a refusal, the applicant may appeal to the Minister of Commerce within 30 days under the International Companies Act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-incorporation corporate governance formalities and bank account activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Directors, registered agent, and licensed offshore bank in Samoa
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The first board of directors convenes (by written resolution or teleconference) to adopt the first board resolution, approve the issue of shares, appoint officers, adopt a corporate seal, and authorize the opening of a bank account for the used machinery trading business. The registered agent files the register of directors and officers with SIFA if required, and annual government fees are settled from the entity's account.
required_dossiers: Minutes of the first board meeting or written resolution
Register of directors, officers and members
Bank account opening bundle (resolution, proof of identity, beneficial ownership statement)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the offshore bank requests further economic substance or source of funds evidence for the used machinery trading activity, the directors supply purchase invoices, end-customer contracts and freight documentation; if SIFA requests annual return filing, the agent cures by filing the return and paying the late fee within 14 days as per the Act.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable (wholesale remarketing of used construction excavators does not require an industrial license in Samoa).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None required for pure trading and remarketing of secondhand heavy machinery.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE), Samoa
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - no manufacturing, extraction, or environmentally hazardous activity is undertaken; the activity is limited to wholesale trading, storage (if any) and sales of used machinery parts.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater, VOC, or stack emissions are generated. If a parts storage warehouse is leased, waste oil and hydraulic-fluid handling must comply with the Waste Management Regulations 2015 and must not be released into drains or soil; any contaminated rags or filters are disposed of through a licensed waste transporter.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate for any occupied office or warehouse from the Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority (SFESA); structural inspection of storage racks and floor loading for heavy-machine components; workplace clearance under the Samoa Occupational Safety and Health Act 2002 for forklift use, lifting gear certification, and first-aid readiness.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry for Revenue (MfR) of Samoa, operating the Tax Administration System (TAS) e-filing portal at www.revenue.gov.ws
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned Samoa International Company (IC) must first obtain its Certificate of Incorporation from the Registrar of International Companies; thereafter it files a Business Registration Application with the Ministry for Revenue, attaching the certificate, constitution, registered-office address in Apia, and notarized director/shareholder identification. The MfR issues a 9-digit Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) and, where required, a separate VAGST registration number within 5 business days of complete submission. Non-resident entities with no Samoan-source income may register for TIN-only status and remain outside the income-tax net.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone - The IC is treated as non-resident and tax-exempt under the International Companies Act 1987 (as amended); it pays only a flat annual government fee and is exempt from income tax, stamp duty, estate duty, and exchange-control approvals, provided no business is transacted within Samoa and no income arises from Samoan sources. Any local-source income (e.g., storage or brokerage connected to Samoan property) becomes assessable under the Income Tax Act 2012.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: The IC may file an irrevocable written election with the Ministry for Revenue to be taxed as an ordinary resident company, thereby forfeiting tax-exempt status and becoming subject to the Income Tax Act 2012 at the then-applicable statutory corporate rate; hybrid-mismatch and US-style check-the-box elections are not recognized. The IC may elect segregated-cell treatment under the International Companies (Amendment) Act 2008 to ring-fence the used-excavator trading pool from other activities, and may elect special-purpose-vehicle status to clarify non-resident tax treatment to counterparties and banks.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Goods and Services Tax (VAGST)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: WST 60,000 of annual taxable turnover - mandatory registration applies to any person making taxable supplies above this threshold in any 12-month period; registration below the threshold is voluntary. Non-resident suppliers of remote/digital or imported services must register if total supplies to Samoan consumers exceed WST 60,000 per annum.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or continuous transaction-control mandate currently applies. VAGST-registered businesses must issue sequentially numbered tax invoices in the prescribed MfR format, file monthly returns through the Tax Administration System (TAS) or its certified API-connected accounting software, and remit net VAGST by the 28th day of the following month; invoice and customs data must be retained for 7 years and are subject to MfR automated risk-scoring and cross-matching with Samoa Customs entry records.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available to a VAGST-registered trader exporting used hydraulic excavators, rollers, and associated earthmoving equipment where the goods are physically exported from Samoa within 28 days of supply under a valid customs export entry, and title passes to a non-resident buyer. Export-related services (e.g., overseas freight brokering, inspection fees invoiced to a foreign buyer, and international arbitration support) are zero-rated if the recipient is a non-resident outside Samoa at the time of supply, the service is performed outside Samoa, and the benefit is enjoyed wholly outside Samoa. The trader must substantiate export status within the filing period and reflect the zero rating in the VAGST return with full documentary retention.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Samoa SAD) with official exit stamp and Customs-coded goods description
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill evidencing delivery to the overseas consignee
Inward Remittance Certificate issued by a licensed commercial bank confirming hard-currency settlement of the export proceeds
Commercial invoice and signed export packing list referencing the IC's TIN and VAGST registration number
Certificate of Origin (where a preferential tariff claim is made) and MfR export clearance certificate
Survey/inspection report (e.g., SGS or equivalent third-party condition report) covering the used machines, to substantiate valuation and arm's-length price
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Samoa Customs and the Ministry for Revenue coordinate through the ASYCUDA World single-window platform; suspected overvaluation or fictitious exports trigger a joint audit. Where zero-rating is disallowed, the MfR assesses VAGST at 15% on the full export consideration, claws back input credits, and applies a late-payment penalty of 50% of the unpaid tax plus interest under the Tax Administration Act 2014. Fraudulent export claims are punishable by an evasion penalty of up to 200% of the tax avoided, public naming of the taxpayer, and imprisonment for up to 7 years; the Customs Service may independently impose forfeiture of the goods and a false-declaration penalty not exceeding WST 100,000 per customs entry.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (Faletupe Tutotonu o Samoa)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Samoan Tālā (WST) is a non-fully-convertible, managed-float currency. Current account transactions, including trade settlements and service payments, are permitted without a general licence but require submission of supporting trade documentation through an authorised dealer. Capital account transactions, including equity injections, share subscriptions, related-party loans, and profit repatriation by non-resident shareholders of a Samoa International Company (IC), require prior written approval or filing with the Central Bank of Samoa under the Exchange Control Act 1976. Remittance of after-tax profits from ICs is generally legally permissible, but the practical hurdles include formal Board-resolved dividend or distribution declarations, audited financial statements evidencing retained earnings, a tax clearance certificate from the Samoa Ministry of Revenue, and confirmation that no outstanding Exchange Control obligations exist. Dividends distributed by an IC whose underlying income is sourced wholly outside Samoa and that is tax-exempt under the International Companies Act 2012 may be remitted without domestic withholding tax, but the Central Bank will still require a signed undertaking that the funds do not derive from any locally prohibited activity.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Exchange Control Regulations, all export receipts from the sale of used construction machinery, excavators, and rollers by a Samoa IC must be repatriated to Samoa and offered for conversion into WST through an authorised dealer within 30 days from the date the foreign currency is credited to an offshore collection account or received by the exporter, whichever occurs first. The mandatory conversion ratio is 100% of the export proceeds unless the Central Bank of Samoa issues a prior exemption certificate permitting the holder to retain the foreign currency for up to 12 months for the direct settlement of verified import obligations or the servicing of approved external debt. For WST-denominated transactions, exporters must declare the value on the applicable Exchange Control form and attach invoices, bills of lading, customs declarations, and proof of physical movement of goods.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of South Pacific Limited – Samoa Branch

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: The prospective viability of offshore fintech Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) is Low. Samoa's legal and regulatory framework does not currently license standalone cross-border digital banks or independent EMIs. An offshore EMI may be used only as a supplementary payment collection instrument, not as a bank-clearing rail, if it is contractually backed by a licensed correspondent bank and it does not hold or intermediate the principal trading account of the Samoa IC. The IC's primary treasury infrastructure must remain anchored in a licensed Samoa commercial bank. Legal constraints include the Central Bank's regulatory advisory powers, the Anti-Money Laundering and Proceeds of Crime Act 2000, and bilateral correspondent-bank compliance expectations under CFATF and FATF standards.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Directors, authorised signatories, and ultimate beneficial owners are generally required to attend a physical, face-to-face bank interview at the onboarding branch in Apia for the initial account activation of non-resident ICs. Remote onboarding is permissible only in exceptional cases, and only when the company uses a registered Samoa corporate-services or trustee licensee with verified AML standing, and where each director's identity is subject to a live video interview, independent biometric verification, notarised identity documents, and an enhanced due-diligence file. For the used heavy-machinery scope, banks will almost always insist on at least one natural-person director or a designated senior manager physically visiting Samoa before any high-value transaction is processed.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ownership combined with a medium-risk wholesale industry involving used construction equipment.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of Incorporation and Certificate of Good Standing issued by the Samoa Companies Registrar; full register of directors, shareholders, and beneficial owners; notarised letters of consent from each director; Ministry of Revenue tax exemption certificate for the IC; current trust or corporate-services licence of the local agent; source-of-initial-funds declaration; and a detailed treasury business plan exhibiting expected counterparties and trade jurisdictions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency cross-border wires in USD for used excavator purchase and remarketing, potentially triggering source-of-wealth concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited or management financial statements of the immediate parent or shareholder; certified underlying sale and purchase contracts for the used hydraulic earthmovers; independent equipment-condition inspection reports; insurance certificates; customs clearance evidence; example bills of lading or airway bills; and a statutory declaration from the beneficial owner tracing the original funding source.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transactions with counterparties located in or involving transshipment through higher-risk jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Copy of the IC's international trade compliance policy; end-user or end-use certificates; original bills of lading and customs entries; import licences from destination countries where applicable; export licences issued by Samoa Customs (if re-exporting from Samoa); a transaction-by-transaction sanctions and debarment screen; and an attestation letter from the local compliance officer confirming no exposure to unlawful or sanctioned end-users.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital construction and equity injections from the parent entity to the Samoa IC must be routed through SWIFT MT103 with a clear sender-to-receiver information line that references 'Samoa International Companies Act 2012 – Share Capital Contribution'. The wire should be directed to the IC's Capital Escrow Account at an authorised dealer bank and must include the IC registration number. The bank will require a certified Board Resolution approving the incoming funds, a share allotment resolution identifying the number and par value of shares issued or treasury shares, a signed source-of-funds declaration from the remitter, and, where triggered, a Central Bank of Samoa Exchange Control consent or post-event notification. For funds above the reporting threshold, the bank must also complete a financial-intelligence filing under the Samoa AML/CFT framework.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements for the purchase of used construction excavators and ancillary equipment must be cleared via one of the following rails, as appropriate: (a) SWIFT MT103 direct transfer for high-value, one-off supplier payments; (b) Commercial Letter of Credit (irrevocable, at-sight or usance) issued by an authorised dealer bank and advised/confirmed through a foreign correspondent bank; and (c) documentary collections (D/P or D/A) for small trade settlements. Each outbound remittance must be supported by the underlying pro-forma invoice, final commercial invoice, transport documents, insurance certificate, and an Exchange Control form. The bank will apply per-transaction verification against the circumvention risk list, sanctioned entities, and the list of countries requiring enhanced due diligence before releasing any USD-denominated payment.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Commercial forward exchange contracts with authorised dealer banks for bona fide trade settlement and/or currency re-export of WST generated from export proceeds

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) executed through an offshore counterparty, subject to Central Bank of Samoa prior notification and permissible only when used to hedge the net currency exposure of a specific confirmed trade transaction

Cross-currency swaps conducted only with a licensed authorised dealer bank after obtaining case-by-case approval from the Central Bank of Samoa, limited to hedge of long-term capital injection or equipment purchase obligations

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: International Company Annual Return and Annual License Fee Renewal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after the anniversary date of incorporation, each year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing attracts a penalty of 10% of the annual fee for each month or part month overdue; if overdue for 3 months, the Registrar may apply to strike the company off the register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Registered Office and Registered Agent Annual Confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the anniversary of incorporation (agent to confirm within the same 30-day window as the annual return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain a registered agent and office in Samoa may result in administrative strike-off and dissolution under the International Companies Act 1987.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No mandatory independent audit for International Companies unless the company is a bank, insurance company, or licensed trustee; wholesale trading of used construction machinery does not trigger compulsory audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: No statutory accounting framework prescribed; IFRS may be adopted voluntarily for management and financing purposes.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No annual UBO filing is required in Samoa; the registered agent must maintain beneficial ownership records for AML/CFT purposes and update the Register of Members promptly upon any share transfer. Changes in shareholding are recorded internally and are not publicly filed.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Memorandum and Articles of Association copy retained at registered office

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not required; voluntary audit would typically cost US$1,500 – US$3,000 per engagement

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (standard Samoa corporate income tax rate for resident companies and branches); 0% effective statutory rate for an International Company (IC) that complies with the International Companies Act 1987 and does not carry on business in Samoa
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Full statutory tax exemption under section 200 of the International Companies Act 1987: no income tax, no dividend withholding tax, no stamp duty, no gift duty, and no estate or succession duty on the offshore trading business of the IC. The only recurring cost is the annual government licence fee payable to the Registrar of International Companies. Samoa also levies no capital gains tax, producing a 0% effective corporate rate on the wholesale margin earned from used construction excavator sales.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual Return of an International Company (IC Act 1987 annual return / Form IC-AR); filed electronically by the licensed Samoan registered agent through the Samoa International Financial Services Authority (SIFSA) Registrar of International Companies online registry portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due within one calendar month following each anniversary of the date of incorporation; the annual government licence fee becomes payable at the same time. The Registrar issues a renewal notice, but no grace period exists for the fee.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Part A — Company Name and Registration Number
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Exact registered corporate name and the unique international company registration number as shown on the Certificate of Incorporation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident owners must reproduce the certificate name exactly; no trading styles, translations or abbreviations are permitted on the register.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Part B — Registered Office and Registered Agent
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Physical street address of the Samoan registered office and the licence number of the registered agent maintaining that office.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident owners cannot nominate a domestic street address; the address of the licensed Samoan registered agent must be used and updated without delay on any change.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Part C — Directors, Secretary and Members
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full names, nationality, residential address and identification numbers of all directors, the corporate secretary and every shareholder or member.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident directors and shareholders must provide certified passports, proof of residential address, and evidence of good standing; nominee holdings must be disclosed to the registered agent.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration identifying every ultimate beneficial owner holding 25% or more of shares or voting rights, with source-of-wealth and source-of-funds statements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Each non-resident UBO must complete customer due diligence and enhanced due diligence forms; if a UBO cannot be identified, the registered agent must file a suspicious transaction report with the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Certification by the directors and registered agent that the IC has not carried on business within Samoa during the reporting year and has otherwise complied with the International Companies Act 1987.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A used-excavator trading IC must verify that negotiation, contracting, invoicing, physical inventory and delivery take place exclusively outside Samoa; if any Samoan-source activity occurred, the IC must declare it and proceed with Ministry for Revenue tax registration.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing and late payment attract a surcharge of 10% of the unpaid licence fee plus a monthly accrual of 2%; continued default beyond six months results in automatic striking-off and dissolution. Directors are jointly liable for outstanding fees, and reinstatement after strike-off requires a court order, payment of all arrears, and a penalty reinstatement fee to the Registrar.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Samoa Income Tax Return — Company (CIT-1 / IRC Form C); filed electronically through the Samoa Ministry for Revenue (MOR) online e-filing and self-assessment portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; quarterly provisional tax instalments are required where the company's residual income exceeds the prescribed threshold under the Tax Administration Act 2007.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within six months after the balance date (for the standard 31 December year-end, the return is due by 30 June of the following year); the Commissioner of Revenue may extend the deadline only on application made before the due date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total consideration from wholesale trading of used construction excavators and rollers, net of returns and discounts; includes all Samoan-source sales and any offshore sales attributable to a Samoan permanent establishment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident traders using an IC that has inadvertently created a Samoan permanent establishment must include only Samoan-source sales in this box; genuine offshore through-sales remain outside the Samoan tax base.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 — Exempt Income and IC Act Exclusions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign-source trading profits of a valid International Company, together with offshore dividends and interest that are exempt under section 200 of the International Companies Act 1987.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach a schedule of exempt IC transactions with supporting sale contracts, bills of lading, inspection certificates and bank statements to demonstrate that no Samoan-source business was conducted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Acquisition cost of the excavators, freight, marine insurance, pre-shipment inspection, customs duties where not creditable, agent commissions, financing costs and overheads incurred directly in deriving assessable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border payments to related suppliers must respect the arm's length principle and be supported by written agreements; the Commissioner may add back non-commercial expenses and adjust transfer pricing margins.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prior-year tax losses carried forward and offset against current net assessable income, subject to the statutory maximum carryforward of five years.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A detailed loss schedule must accompany the return; continuity of ownership and same-business tests apply whenever non-resident shareholders change during the loss period.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 — Taxable Income and Tax Payable
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income multiplied by the 25% corporate rate, reduced by foreign withholding tax credits, provisional tax paid, and any authorised credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident IC that becomes taxable must appoint a Samoan tax agent and, if it employs staff or imports machinery into Samoa, must also register for PAYE and value-added/goods and services tax.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: civil penalty of 10% of unpaid tax plus 2% monthly surcharge; under-declaration penalties of 20% for failure to take reasonable care, 40% for gross carelessness and 75% for an abusive tax position; wilful evasion attracts a 150% shortfall penalty and criminal prosecution. Directors become personally liable where the company is unable to pay the assessed amounts.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% for dividends paid by an International Company: section 200 of the International Companies Act 1987 exempts all IC dividends from Samoan income tax and withholding tax, so no non-resident dividend WHT arises on distributions from a compliant IC. The standard Samoa statutory non-resident dividend WHT is 15% but applies only to resident trading companies, never to a compliant IC distribution.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Samoa has a limited DTA network limited principally to Commonwealth and Pacific partners (including Australia, New Zealand, Fiji, Tonga, Papua New Guinea and several smaller Pacific island states) plus a Tax Information Exchange Agreement with the United States. Because the IC itself pays no Samoan tax, treaty relief is normally invoked in the counterparty jurisdiction: (i) obtain an official proof of IC status or, where the payer demands a treaty residence certificate, apply to the Samoa Ministry for Revenue for a Certificate of Residence (TRC); (ii) deliver the certificate together with the payer's own treaty claim form (e.g., Form 6166 or the local equivalent); (iii) attach the relevant DTA article limiting dividend, interest or royalty rates; and (iv) claim the reduced rate at source or, where tax has been overwithheld, seek a refund through the source country's administrative procedure. Inbound treaty relief for a non-resident investing in a taxable Samoan entity is claimed by filing a Samoan income tax return with the Ministry for Revenue and attaching the DTA and the foreign tax authority's certificate of residence.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory non-resident final withholding tax on Samoan-source interest and royalties is 15% each; treaty rates under Samoan DTAs generally reduce interest and royalty WHT to 10%, and certain treaty dividends to 0-5% depending on shareholding thresholds. A compliant IC pays no Samoan WHT on outbound offshore royalty or interest flows because such income is not Samoan-source; however, if the IC transacts inside Samoa or a taxable Samoan entity is involved, a 15% statutory WHT applies unless treaty relief is approved in advance.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No statutory Local File or Master File thresholds exist under Samoan law; the arm's length rule in section 79 of the Income Tax Act 2007 applies only to taxable resident entities. As a risk-based benchmark, a used-excavator International Company engaged in related-party transactions should prepare a contemporaneous transfer pricing memorandum where annual related-party turnover exceeds WST 2,000,000 (approximately USD 740,000) or where a single related-party excavator sale exceeds WST 500,000; below these thresholds a concise contract-and-margin note is maintained. The Samoan exemption does not relieve the IC of the need to evidence arm's length pricing in the customer's high-tax jurisdiction.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Samoa does not operate a codified Economic Substance Regulations regime comparable to the UAE or the BVI; there is no ESR filing and no substance score. Instead, Samoa enforces substance through the International Companies Act 1987 prohibition against carrying on business in Samoa, the annual compliance certificate, mandatory beneficial ownership reporting, and AML/CFT supervision by the Central Bank of Samoa. Internationally, downstream tax authorities will apply OECD BEPS Action 5, controlled foreign company rules, substance-over-form, and general anti-abuse rules to challenge a used-excavator trading IC that lacks genuine management, staff, decision-making, a real bank account, inventory risk, and operational function outside Samoa. The IC must therefore maintain a demonstrable commercial role in the market where the functions are performed, such as actual dealer inventory, inspection yard exposure, credit risk, and independent negotiation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a letterbox Samoan International Company that books the entire used-excavator resale margin while negotiation, custody, customs filing, billing and bank accounts remain in the customer's jurisdiction, and then making false declarations to the Registrar to preserve the 0% tax status.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Up to a 150% evasion shortfall penalty plus interest under the Tax Administration Act 2007; criminal conviction attracts fines up to WST 1,000,000 and/or imprisonment up to seven years. The customer-country tax authority may reassess the economic owner on the full resale margin, deny DTA benefits, and impose additional foreign penalties and interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Courts will pierce the corporate veil where the IC is a mere facade: directors and ultimate beneficial owners become jointly and severally liable for the unpaid tax, interest and penalties; asset-freeze orders and travel bans are available in Samoa and through mutual assistance channels; imprisonment and director disqualification of up to ten years may follow.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining an IC with no office, no employees, no demonstrable decision-making, no real bank account activity, and no evidence of where purchase, inventory, marketing, pricing and risk decisions are made for the excavator trading business.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Deregistration and striking-off by the Registrar of International Companies under the International Companies Act 1987; in the destination state, application of CFC and anti-avoidance rules, reallocation of profit to the beneficial owner, imposition of tax at the applicable corporate rate, penalties and late-interest, and denial of tax residence certificates. The EU and OECD framework may classify the IC as a shell with no entitlement to treaty benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Director disqualification in Samoa and in the customer jurisdiction; personal assessment for the tax reallocated where the corporate entity is dissipating assets; cross-border recovery against foreign director assets; visa and immigration restrictions in multiple treaty partner jurisdictions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML/CFT Violations (Beneficial Ownership and Wire / SWIFT LC Flows)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to identify the ultimate beneficial owner before accepting large wire transfers or SWIFT letters of credit for excavator sales, concealing beneficial ownership, transacting with sanctioned parties, processing funds with grossly inconsistent source-of-funds documentation, or allowing the Samoan registered agent to remain passive while suspicious funds move through the IC account.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Samoa's AML/CFT Act, corporate fines of up to WST 1,000,000 and individual fines of up to WST 500,000; mandatory suspicious transaction reporting, transaction freeze orders, confiscation of the excavator sale proceeds, and forced termination of the registered agency relationship leading to deregistration of the IC.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the appointed Money Laundering Reporting Officer face imprisonment of up to fourteen years for money laundering offences; personal confiscation orders, travel bans, listing on sanctions databases, and permanent prohibition from managing any Samoan international company or trust.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Fraud / False Intercompany Margin
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Pricing used excavators to a related Samoan IC at an artificially low export price, inflating intercompany purchase costs from group suppliers, or paying management and commission fees to a related shell so that the taxable operating company reports a thin margin in the high-tax destination while the exempt IC accumulates the profit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: In Samoa, where the entity is taxable, the Commissioner may adjust the price to the arm's length standard, impose shortfall penalties of 20% to 150% and interest; in the destination market, primary adjustments, corresponding dividend or royalty withholding taxes, late-interest and penalties of 10% to 100% may apply. Mutual agreement procedure under the relevant DTA can relieve double taxation only if both tax administrations accept the adjustment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false transfer pricing disclosures face personal fines, perjury referral, and joint liability for the adjusted tax where the company is judgment-proof; repeated wilful conduct is prosecuted as tax evasion and may result in custodial sentences.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Breach of IC Tax-Exempt Status (Carrying on Business in Samoa)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The IC leases office space in Apia, employs Samoan staff, warehouses, inspects or repairs excavators in Samoa, issues invoices from Samoa, or holds board meetings in Samoa, any of which constitutes carrying on business in Samoa and voids the statutory tax exemption.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The IC immediately becomes taxable in Samoa on its Samoan-source income at 25%, with mandatory tax registration, a 10% late-filing penalty, monthly interest at 2%, and up to a 150% evasion penalty for concealment; the Registrar may compulsorily convert the IC to a domestic company or strike it off the register.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who certify the annual compliance certificate while knowing business was conducted in Samoa commit a false declaration offence: a fine of up to WST 20,000 plus imprisonment under the Tax Administration Act; personal liability is imposed for all unpaid corporate tax and penalties of the company.
